messages:
Anya: Heads-up — ran a night-run of the continuous-batcher trace on prod-sim and we're seeing persistent throughput skew: short-seq tenants get ~2-3x more mini-batches served per unit token than long-seq tenants. Not just latency — cost/throughput fairness is off.
Sam: Interesting. Any KV-hit distribution differences? short seqs often have higher kv-hit rate which could bias credit refill.
Anya: Yeah, KV hit skew is part of it. Short sequences get a lot of prefix cache hits so they finish earlier and consume fewer credits; the allocator then tops up others faster and they steal more batch slots. That loop amplifies the imbalance.
MJ: Do we have profiling from the kernel selector path? If kernel affinity favors short sequences (optimized kernels for short lengths) that also speeds them up relative to long ones.
Anya: Good call — profiler shows kernel-choice divergence at sequence-length ~128. Short lanes hit a fast GEMM kernel that completes <6ms on our cards, long lanes go to the fallback matmul that runs ~22ms.
Kevin: InfraBot reported a small regression yesterday on the long-seq tail — looks correlated with the rollout that changed the batch-coalescer merge window (PR #5367).
InfraBot: deploy-bot: Rollout 2026-04-02T07:11: triggering canary -> 4/8 hosts. Observability alert: 95th latency for model-x long sequences increased by 18%.
Sam: We should try 'slicing credit allocator' — split token budget into N slices per tenant per epoch so long/short sequences get reserved micro-quotas. That prevents immediate starvation when short sequences spike.
Dina: Can you sketch config? I'll run A/B in the staging fleet.
Sam: Proposed config snippet (pseudo):
```
batcher.slice_count = 8
batcher.slice_size_tokens = tenant.tokens_per_min / slice_count
batcher.slice_refill_ms = 250
batcher.slice_priority = [latency_priority, fairness_boost]
```
Sam: Behavior: each slice accrues credits up to slice_size_tokens. When a slice is used by a request it decays, refill is per-slice so a tenant can't consume all slices instantly.
Anya: Also want to add 'kernel affinity balancing' — inject a lightweight scheduler that tags long sequences and gives them occasional priority windows (e.g., 1/10 batches are long-only). That smooths tail latency without say removing short perf.
MJ: Need telemetry additions before we flip. Metrics we need: per-tenant slice occupancy, per-length kernel-choice counter, kv-hit ratio by lane, and inter-batch wait time histogram.
Dina: I'll add those to staging logging. Recommend a metric name namespace: runtime.slice_occupancy, runtime.kernel_choice, cache.kv_hit_by_len, batch.wait_ms_hist.
Sam: One more thought — batch coalescing window tuning: smaller windows reduce long/short intermixing but hurt utilization. We can make it adaptive: if long-tail latency > threshold, shrink coalescer for N seconds.
Anya: Agreed. Let's combine approaches: 1) slicing credit allocator as guardrails, 2) kernel-affinity micro-windows, 3) adaptive coalescer tie to tail SLO.
Kevin: Danger: all three together could oscillate. We need a safety interlock: a global dampener that prevents >2 config flips per 5m and a rollback trigger if 95p latency worsens by >10%.
MJ: Also check KV cache heatmap — if long sequences are cold, warming policies (prefetch last-kv for pinned tenants) can help without changing scheduling.
Dina: Plan for staging run: A) baseline collect 2h, B) enable slice allocator only 2h, C) add kernel windows 2h, D) combine adaptive coalescer 2h. I'll run on the canary group and collect metrics.
Anya: I'll prepare the experiment YAML and the rollout playbook (including rollback gating). Also capturing sample traces for offline replay.
Sam: Can we add a simple fairness score metric: fairness = median(tokens_served_per_tenant)/p95(tokens_served_per_tenant) (closer to 1 is better). Hook as alert if <0.6.
Kevin: Good idea. Add to SLO dashboard.
Dina: Kicking off staging at 09:00 PT. Will post updates. :rocket:
Anya: Thanks team. If staging looks good, we can canary to 10% next week and monitor the fairness metric + model-quality regressions.
Sam: One micro-note — watch for quantization kernel regressions when we change kernel hints; add a unit test that runs model-x with quantized path on short/long synthetic traffic.
MJ: I'll author the unit test.
InfraBot: perf-alert: Background sweep detected unusual queue build for tenant-b: queue-depth spike 2026-04-02T09:14. Investigating.
Dina: Noted, will correlate.
Anya: Closing loop: doc and playbook in PR later today. Thanks.
